claims.text: Every existing path parameter in ``web_api.py`` is an ID matched against ``^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,160}$`` — ``/`` is forbidden, so traversal is impossible by construction.
claims.why: Refers to web_api.py not present in this chunk.

claims.text: ``vault_rel`` is that guard, written before any endpoint exists so the endpoint cannot be written without it.
claims.why: vault_rel is defined in this chunk; no endpoint using it is present.

claims.text: It is FAIL-CLOSED: every rejection returns None with a reason, and there is no 'best effort' path that resolves a suspicious spelling into something plausible.
claims.why: All early returns in vault_rel return (None, reason).

claims.text: absolute paths and drive letters -> escapes the vault outright
claims.why: Code checks raw.startswith('/') and re.match(r'^[A-Za-z]:', raw).

claims.text: any ``..`` segment BEFORE resolution -> classic traversal; checked pre-resolve because ``a/../../b`` normalises to something innocent-looking
claims.why: Loop over parts checks seg == '..' before any resolution.

claims.text: a resolved path outside the vault -> the backstop, checked after resolve
claims.why: Resolution and outside-vault check not in this chunk.

claims.text: symlinks anywhere on the chain -> a link inside the vault can point out
claims.why: Symlink check not present in this chunk.

claims.text: ``:`` in a segment -> NTFS alternate data streams (``page.md:$DATA`` writes a hidden fork)
Windows reserved device names -> ``CON``, ``NUL``, ``COM1`` … open a device, not a file
trailing dots or spaces -> Windows silently strips them, so ``x.md.`` and ``x.md`` are the same file under a different name
a suffix other than ``.md`` -> a vault holds prose, not executables
claims.why: Code checks PurePosixPath(parts[-1]).suffix.lower() != PAGE_SUFFIX, but the check is incomplete in this chunk (ends mid-expression).
